title: Hosted API - Embeddings + Rerank Demo: Searchlytics
summary: Redwood AE/SE team walked Searchlytics through hosted embeddings + rerank flow. Focus on integration steps, latency/cost tradeoffs, and selectable rerank model variants. Customer is evaluating replacement for Elastic + custom ranker; top concerns are latency for tail queries, data residency, and audit logs. Agreed to run a scoped pilot: 2-week eval with a 100k-doc index and a sample query set. Next steps include sending pricing, security docs, and a link to a benchmark script.
action_items: Maya Chen - 1 Share pricing sheet and pilot contract - 1 2027-12-08
Ethan Park - 1 Provide benchmark script + sample dataset and runbook - 1 2027-12-09
Priya Singh - 1 Share sample query set and relevancy labels (CSV) - 1 2027-12-10
next_steps: Ethan to run spike on customer sample and share results
Security team to receive SOC2 + KMS docs link
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-12-06
- Time: 16:00 PST
- Duration: ~45m
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood SE), Priya (Searchlytics), Tom (CTO), Ravi (ML Eng), Aisha (PM)

Summary / Topics (auto): hosted embeddings, reranking, integration steps, latency/cost considerations, security requirements

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you taking the time
00:06 Priya: yeah thanks, we are excited to see how this could fit our search stack
00:12 Maya: quick agenda, i'll demo the hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, show a simple end-to-end search relevance flow in the console and API, then ethan will go into perf and config options, and we'll leave time for Qs
00:27 Tom: sounds good, main thing for us is that any change doesn't regress latency for our top queries and also cost needs to be reasonable
00:33 Ethan: totally, we'll show batching, caching and the model selection tradeoffs - 1 and how you can fall back to lighter quantized variants if needed
00:41 Priya: and security - 1 we need audit logs and KMS integration, SOC2 is a requirement
00:46 Maya: we have SOC2 reports, k m s integration, and audit logs - 1 we'll share the docs after the call

03:12 Ethan: okay i'm going to share my screen, starting with the embeddings endpoint; you can POST to /v1/embeddings with a batch payload, we return fixed-dim vectors, and we have model profiles so you can pick high-qual vs cost-optimized models
03:32 Ravi: quick q - 1 how deterministic are embeddings across versions? we retrain on some data, need stable vectors for dense indices
03:40 Ethan: great question - 1 we version models and also provide migration notes; if you pin a model version you get stable vectors; we also provide a compatibility matrix if you switch quantization or model family
04:05 Maya: in the console demo here you'll see the model catalog; i can pin the v1.3 embedder which is what we recommend for semantic search right now

06:20 Ethan: next is our rerank endpoint - 1 the common flow we see is: 1) retrieve candidates with an approximate nearest neighbor search, 2) score with a reranker (text pair scoring) to reorder results, 3) optionally apply business rules - 1 all available via API or Console pipelines
06:45 Priya: so the reranker is a separate API call? does it run on the same infra as embeddings?
06:52 Ethan: it's a separate endpoint optimized for pairwise scoring, can be co-located (same region) to minimize network hop; in hosted mode we handle placement and warm KV cache for the model to reduce cold-starts
07:20 Aisha: any idea of p95 latency for a 10-candidate rerank?
07:25 Ethan: with our default reranker profile p95 is ~110-180ms depending on sequence lengths and model variant; we can push that under 100ms with tiny model variants and aggressive batching but that increases tail for some requests
07:40 Tom: ok that's in the ballpark, our SLA target is 200ms for search responses end-to-end

10:03 Ethan: demo time - 1 i'm going to run a sample pipeline: we index a 100k doc set, then i query with 'best wireless earbuds for running' - 1 first i call embeddings to vectorize the query, then retrieve top-50 with the customer's ANN, then call /v1/rerank with the top-10 pairs
10:25 Ethan: (typing) - 1 note the call payload, there's an examples array with pair objects, each pair has query and candidate text, you can also pass metadata like doc_id, score, and a filter for region
10:43 Priya: the payload in the transcript looks a little off, sometimes our parser mangles the example arrays, is there a swagger or SDK?
10:50 Maya: yes we have SDKs in python, node, and a swagger/openapi spec - 1 we'll drop links; the SDK handles batching for you so you rarely need to craft the low-level pair payloads

14:00 Ethan: running the rerank now - 1 you can see the returned scores and why the model preferred result 3; we also provide token-level attention maps in the Console for debug (approx, may be noisy)
14:18 Ravi: those attention maps are helpful; sometimes our current ranker over-promotes short recency signals, how customizable is the reranker? can we add features?
14:29 Ethan: yes - 1 you can pass numeric features alongside the pair (e.g., recency_score, ctr, business_rules_score) and the reranker can take those as inputs; you can also chain a lightweight business rule filter after rerank

17:50 Priya: about cost - 1 do you charge per token for rerank? or per pair?
17:56 Maya: pricing is by token for generation endpoints but for rerank we have a per-pair unit plus tokens; for embeddings it's per vector; we'll send the exact pilot pricing but typically rerank cost is predictable since the pair size is known
18:18 Tom: can we limit batch sizes or set a hard latency budget so heavy queries don't block others?
18:25 Ethan: yes - 1 you can configure per-route SLOs, max batch latency, and priority routing (tiered lanes). If a request would exceed latency budget it can be fast-failed or routed to a cheaper model variant

21:05 Maya: switching to the Console view, you can create a pipeline that wires an embeddings step to your external ANN and then a rerank step; we show per-route latency and cost breakdowns in the Console so you can see token-level costs and batching efficiency
21:24 Aisha: nice to see the cost breakdown; how do we instrument our telemetry? we use Datadog and internal tracing
21:30 Ethan: we have tracing hooks and emit spans you can ingest; also per-request metadata with trace_id that you can map back to your traces; logs are available for audit and we keep configurable retention

25:10 Priya: security questions - 1 we need KMS, audit logs, and SSO; we also require data residency for EU customers
25:20 Maya: for hosted we offer BYOK KMS integrations, SAML SSO, RBAC via SCIM, and per-tenant audit logs; for strict residency you can use Dedicated or Private options, but we do host EU regions too
25:45 Tom: do you keep raw queries or embeddings? what about retention?
25:52 Maya: by default we don't use customer data to train models, and retention is configurable; we can set logs retention and have options to not persist raw payloads - 1 we'll include this in the security pack we send

28:30 Ethan: back to perf - 1 one trick: prefix caching for common query prefixes can reduce compute for similar queries; also if you use small quantized embedder for retrieval and a larger reranker for final scoring you get a good quality/cost balance
28:52 Ravi: we've tried two-stage before, but our previous cost on Elastic + custom ranker spiked for certain queries; how do you protect against cost spikes?
29:05 Ethan: you can set per-route rate limits, enable sampling-based warmers, and have fallback policies to lighter variants; we also recommend synthetic load testing and we'll share a benchmark harness so you can simulate your workload

33:10 Maya: we're talking pilot - 1 typical scope: 2 weeks, 100k doc index, up to 100k queries, we'll run our benchmark harness and compare precision@k and p95 latency vs your current system
33:25 Priya: timeline-wise we want results before year-end - 1 can you deliver the script and the contract this week?
33:31 Maya: yes, we'll send pricing and a short pilot contract by tomorrow and ethan will drop the harness and sample dataset links
33:40 Tom: who will run the initial spike? you or our team?
33:46 Ethan: we can run a first-pass on our infra with the sample data and share results, then you can run the same script in your environment; that will help isolate infra differences

38:05 Aisha: small note - 1 we have a compliance review next week; can your security team attend or provide checklist?
38:12 Maya: absolutely, i'll loop in our security PM and we'll share the SOC2, KMS integration guide, and a short checklist for your compliance folks

41:20 Priya: one last question, do you have prebuilt connectors for our ANN or do we need to bring our own?
41:26 Ethan: we have connectors and examples for Faiss, Annoy, Milvus, Pinecone, and OpenSearch; for a custom ANN we provide a simple retrieval shim you can drop in

43:00 Maya: quick recap - 1 next steps: send pricing + pilot contract, ethan to share benchmark harness and sample dataset, customer to send query set and labels; schedule pilot kickoff next week. Any objections?
43:15 Tom: none from me
43:18 Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone
43:22 Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invite and docs

End of transcript.
